title: Siegard conformance return
description: One specification-conformance-reviewer delegation's answer, as a file. The agent returns this mapping as plain YAML text; the caller saves it verbatim, one file per delegation, under `siegard-reconcile/<slug>.returns/` — the returns are the evidence a reconciliation record is folded from, and a judgment whose raw answer survives nowhere is a judgment the record's reader cannot reopen. `bin/trace.py --fold` validates every return against this contract and refuses a delegation whose answer does not hold: an unusable return means the prompt was wrong, and the correction is a fresh delegation, never a repair applied to the answer by whoever saved it. A finding's own fields are the delivery-node contract's `finding` shape minus `pass` — the caller knows which pass it delegated, and a return cannot claim a pass that did not run.

specNodeRef.description: A specification node, by identity — «Identity is the node's path from the specification root, without `.md`» (SPEC-003 R1).

findings.description: What the judgment found against, with the evidence quoted. Absent entirely where nothing was found — an absent key is a real result and a claim: over this file and these nodes, the source states what the specification holds and nothing else.

file.description: The path the finding was observed in, exactly as the file set lists it — spelled from the target source root, the anchor every record in this framework uses. A reconciliation delegation reads one file and its node pack header names the spelling; stated here, it must match.

where.description: The line, or the construct, within the file.

evidence.description: Quoted from the source, never restated. Where the finding is an absence, this quotes the construct that should have held the fact.

cost.description: The consequence, in terms a reader can weigh — never only the rule it broke.

kind.description: Which question this finding answers, because the pair's own conformance and the specification's completeness are two of them and one word settles which. `contradicts` — the source says what this node denies, or no longer carries the fact it holds: the pair is the subject, and the act is on the pair, so the node does not bind. `unstated` — the source states a fact no node holds at all: the specification is the subject, the route is the analysis that gives the fact a node, and no rebind can ever close it, so it never blocks a binding the node's own reading cleared. Where both are true of one file, they are two findings, because they are owed to two people.

correction.description: What would have to change; omitted where the judge cannot say.

node.description: The node this is about, where one node owns it — a candidate's identity where the fact is a candidate's rather than the set's. Omitted where no node holds it, and the fold then holds every node of this file's set to the finding: an unattributed finding is conservative by design, and the price of that default is carried by the file that produced it.

read.description: One entry per node of the delegation's own set, in the order the set gave them — exactly that set, never a subset and never a candidate. It is a different statement from `findings`: per node, what was read and where the node's fact sits now. The fold writes a cleared node's `how` from this and from nothing else.

held_at.description: Where in the file the node's fact sits now, or the word `nowhere`. A fact is held by code, never by prose about it: a comment restating the node is `nowhere` with a finding saying what the comment claims.

evidence.description: Quoted from the source — what was read to say that; code, never a comment's claim. Where `held_at` is `nowhere`, this quotes what was looked at.

looked_past.description: One sentence naming what was seen and not reported because it is another judgment's. Omitted where there was nothing.

candidates_opened.description: Every candidate node the delegation actually opened, whether or not a finding came of it. Omitted where none was. This is the one field that measures the candidate tier: what was offered is in the delegation's prompt, what was used is here, and the distance between the two is what a later reading of the returns can weigh.

read.held_at: the return statement of place(), line 41

findings.where: the guard added to raise(), line 12
findings.cost: the at-most-one-invoice rule lives only here, so the next reader looks for it in the specification and does not find it

read.evidence: the rule the file cites governs modification of a raised invoice; `if (order.invoices.length >= 1)` states a cap no node holds
